text: I’m Dr. Fade. I’ll show you around, help you build your first gang, and stay beside you through your first win. One move at a time.
No timer. No purchases. We’ll learn by playing.
Your Safehouse is where you return between fights. The objects in this room open the parts of your game.
The TV, speakers, and console sit along the left wall, beside your record player. Tap Story. That’s your main adventure: dialogue, battles, new cards, and chapter rewards.
Start with Chapter 1. Follow the highlighted scene, then the next. New chapters open as you clear the story.
Tap Back to the room. Let’s get you familiar with the place before we build your gang.
That record player beside the TV is Fade Tunes. Open Records when you want to pick the soundtrack for your Safehouse.
Buddy’s Growth Lab is tucked into the back-left corner. Check in there for your daily rewards and keep your streak growing.
See that metal bookshelf under the blackboard? The portrait beside the little fist trophy opens your profile. That’s who you represent on the block.

That big wooden door in the back-right corner is your mail. When it knocks, you have something unread. Open it and the Mailman brings your letters and gifts. Read each letter, then claim any gift inside. No codes needed.
Your bag keeps track of your Clout, Pack Tickets, Style Shards, and collection. Fade Market is where you put those resources to work.
The hanging heavy bag opens Training. Come here to practice your plays and try out a gang before you take it into a fight.

The Fadecade is at the other end of the couch. That arcade machine takes you to challenges like Straight to the Back and Stockz. Its screen says Play New Game when you’re starting fresh, or Continue when you have a run waiting.
The phone beside the couch opens online play. When you’re ready, use it to challenge a friend.
The Bounties badge opens your missions. Check your goals, finish the job, and claim the rewards you’ve earned.
Tap Gang. Your collection is every card you own. Your deck is the ten cards you take into a battle.
I have a free starter collection for you, including Cornball, Plug, Snow Bunny, and my Legendary card. We’ll start with ten, make one swap together, and save your gang.
Watch close. You’re next.
Play him for 4 Motion. He brings 6 Hands, hits the strongest enemy in his district for −2 Hands, and gives your weakest ally in another district +2 Hands.
We’ll save him for your first SQUABBLE: 12 base Hands in one play. Follow the highlights and see it happen.
These ten cards are your battle lineup. The first five are your opening hand. Tap the highlighted sixth slot to change a later draw.
Tap Landlord. The number at the top is its Motion cost; Hands is the strength it adds to a district. This card replaces your selected slot.
You made your first swap. Save your gang and take it into a guided match. I’ll point to every move.
Tap Plug. It costs 1 Motion in our target district. Hands is the strength it adds to your side.
Tap this district. You win by leading in two of the three districts at the end. Your first play here costs 1 less Motion (minimum 1). Discounts do not stack.
The preview shows the known score after your card lands. Play the card to resolve it now.
Your card is on the board. Tap End Turn. In regular battles, you can play more cards first if you have enough Motion.
Tap Wifey. It costs 3 Motion in our target district. Hands is the strength it adds to your side.
Tap this district. You win by leading in two of the three districts at the end. Spread your strength instead of putting everyone in one place.
The preview shows the known score after your card lands. Play the card to resolve it now.
Your card is on the board. Tap End Turn. In regular battles, you can play more cards first if you have enough Motion.
Tap End Turn without playing. One unused Motion carries into the next round. Watch your Motion counter when the next round starts.
Tap Dr. Fade. He brings 6 Hands, hits the strongest enemy here for −2, and gives your weakest ally in another district +2.
Tap SQUABBLE. It doubles his base Hands from 6 to 12. His punch and coaching ability still resolve.
Tap THE TRAP. Dr. Fade fights here while helping an ally in another district. Watch both scores.
Confirm your play. Dr. Fade lands with 12 base Hands, then his ability resolves. You keep this Legendary after the lesson.
Your card is on the board. Tap End Turn. In regular battles, you can play more cards first if you have enough Motion.
You secured at least two districts. Change one card and compare how often its ability helps you hold that second district.
Your first fade is saved. You built a gang, played cards, banked Motion, and used SQUABBLE. Chapter 1 is next.
Keep what worked. Change what didn’t. Every card in your collection can be part of your next idea.
The number at the top is its Motion cost; Hands is the strength it adds to a district. This card replaces your selected slot.
Hands is the strength it adds to your side.
Tap this district. You win by leading in two of the three districts at the end.
Dr. Fade fights here while helping an ally in another district. Watch both scores.

Tap Gang. Your collection is every card you own. Your deck is ten different cards from that collection. The first five are your opening hand, then you draw one new card each round from round two through six.
Your lineup needs ten different cards you own. Hold a card to inspect it without playing it. Tap the highlighted sixth slot to plan a swap.
Choose an owned recruit. Check its Motion cost, Base Hands, and ability before deciding. Compare your new card with the one it would replace.
Confirm the swap when you're ready.
The new card keeps that draw position. Your gang is ready. Save it, then let's review the goal before your first fight.
Finish ahead in at least two of the three districts to win. A tie belongs to neither side. The rival plays at the top of the board; your gang plays at the bottom.
This is a four-round, timer-free lesson with a limited rival. Regular fights usually last six rounds, and their rules or clocks may differ.
Choose the highlighted card. Motion pays for the play. Base Hands add strength to a district. Inspect the other lit cards if you want to see your options.
Choose the highlighted district, read its rule, and compare the Rival and You scores. You need two district leads when the match ends.
The preview estimates what happens on the board you can see. It cannot promise what the rival will do next. Confirm your play.
You can play more affordable cards before ending a normal turn. In this coached round, tap End Turn and watch the rival respond.
Hold up. That was the rival's move. Check the card and what changed on the board. Tap Continue the play when you're ready.
Every district changes the fight. Choose an affordable card, then check where its ability and the district rule will help most.
Spread your strength. A big lead in one district cannot replace a lead in a second one.
Tap the selected card again to clear it. Then end your turn without playing.
End Turn without playing. At most one unused Motion carries into the next round's refill. Watch your Motion counter.
Tap Dr. Fade. His Base Hands help hold this district. His ability can hit the strongest enemy here and coach a weak ally somewhere else, if those cards are present.
Tap SQUABBLE. It adds Dr. Fade's Base Hands again before other bonuses. You can do that once per match, and it costs no extra Motion.
Put Dr. Fade in the highlighted district. Read its rule.
Confirm your play. The preview includes known effects, but not the rival's next answer.
Dr. Fade stays in your collection after this lesson.
Your SQUABBLE is spent. End the turn and see whether the rival can answer those doubled Base Hands.
If you already used SQUABBLE, read the scores and play this round your way.
Check each district's final score. A tied district belongs to neither side. District claims decide the winner, not total Hands across the board.
Your ten-card gang and chosen cover are saved. You can review your lineup before another fade.
Your starter cards are already yours. Your welcome reward is ready to claim. A practice fight does not claim it.

Clout pays for eligible purchases and coaching. Profile XP grows your account level. Street Rep tracks separate account progress. Character XP belongs to an individual card. Pack tickets open packs. Style Shards unlock cosmetic styles, not extra Hands or Motion.
You can practice with your saved gang or head into Chapter One.
Keep what worked, change what didn't, and take your next idea onto the block.
Burn stacks remove that many Hands at round end, then the stacks clear. Cleanse it before round end or plan around the coming score loss.
A Frozen card adds 0 Hands and its ability cannot fire until it is cleansed. A frozen card still occupies its district, so a cleanse can bring it back online.
Cleanse removes Burn, Freeze, Silence, Weaken, and Lock from a card. Friendly buffs such as protection and Boost stay in place.
Protection blocks a targeted hostile effect. Some shields last for the round; Cover lasts until spent. Use protection before the rival targets your most valuable fighter.
The incoming targeted effect was stopped, so its intended change did not land. The protection that stopped it may now be spent; check the card status before the next attack.
A Weakened card keeps its Hands but cannot fire its ability. Cleanse restores the ability. The card can still help hold its district meanwhile.
A Silenced card keeps its Hands but cannot fire its ability. Play for its raw Hands or cleanse it before you need the ability.
An ability moved a card to another district after it was already in play. Recheck both district scores after movement; one move can swing two districts.
A Locked card cannot be moved to another district until it is cleansed. Its Hands still count where it stands. Cleanse it if repositioning matters.
A Boosted card gains +1 Hands at every round end while Boost remains active. Early Boosts compound over several rounds, so answer them before they grow.
Welcome to recruitment. You hit the bag, somebody joins your gang. Finally, a gym membership with benefits.
First one's on me. This welcome ticket guarantees Dr. Fade. Yes, me. I handled the booking.
Tap the bag for a jab. We're opening a pack, not filing a complaint.
Good. Now give it a hook. Turn that shoulder.
One more. Put some neighborhood in it!
Surprise. It's the man on the ticket. Dr. Fade, reporting for gang duty.
Already got me? That copy turns into Style Shards. Same handsome doctor, something useful for your collection.
That's a pull. This welcome ticket was guaranteed. Regular packs use the drop rates. Check those before you spend, then take your gang outside.
